rowText.steps: On a turn with a fold row: Down from the question's Retry reaches the row (no skip); Up from the answer's first stop reaches the row; Down from the row enters the answer; the ring is visible above the dock at each of those; nothing traps: from the row, Up, Up, Up reaches the tab strip or the chat slot row within five presses.
rowText.expected: The new fold-row stop fits cleanly into the existing D-pad graph with no traps.

deviation: Down from Retry needs two presses to reach the fold row (an intermediate question-row-body stop sits between them), not one as a strict reading of 'no skip' might imply -- see REASONING-02 for the same finding. Everything else matched.

reads.note: Retry -> Down -> Down reached the fold row; rect bottom 244.6 vs dock top 297.2 -- visible above the dock.
From inside the open answer, Up reached the fold row directly (1 press).
Down from the fold row entered the answer bubble (bonsai-answer-stop class), not Retry and not the dock.
From the fold row: Up, Up, Up (3 presses, within the 5-press budget) reached the chat-slot row (class bonsai-chat-slot-row-focus) -- no trap.

verdictSentence: The new reasoning row sits cleanly in the D-pad path -- reachable from the question and the answer on both sides, always above the bottom dock, and backing out with Up three times lands safely on the chat-slot row with no dead end; reaching it going down from the Retry icon takes one extra press because the question's own row is in between.
